title: Classiq Updates Qmod Compiler to Synthesize 2048-Bit Shor’s Algorithm in Under 10 Seconds - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Classiq upgraded its Qmod language and synthesis compiler so the period-finding subroutine of Shor's algorithm for a 2048-bit RSA-scale integer compiles in under ten seconds, by preserving classical control structures and symbolic qubit indexing instead of flattening circuits.

insights.claim: Classiq's updated Qmod compiler synthesizes the period-finding subroutine of Shor's algorithm for a 2048-bit RSA-scale integer in under ten seconds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removes a software tooling bottleneck for fault-tolerant-era programs; strengthens Classiq's position in quantum software.

insights.claim: Flat circuit representations in fault-tolerant quantum tooling unroll classical loops and duplicate subroutines, causing synthesis runtimes and program sizes to blow up as qubit counts grow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compiler architecture, not just hardware, is a scaling constraint — favours vendors with structured/high-level synthesis.
insights.locator: Detailed in a technical post by Classiq’s Matan Vax

insights.claim: Classiq's Qmod compiler preserves classical control structures (repeat, foreach, conditionals) through synthesis and lets classical iteration variables symbolically index qubit arrays, so arithmetic modules, QFT and QPE synthesize in nearly constant time with respect to operand width.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Near-constant-time synthesis versus width is the key technical moat claim to monitor against competing compilers.

insights.claim: Qmod keeps the coprime base a as a runtime execution parameter, so one compiled Shor program can be reused across multiple Shor iterations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compile-once, run-many reduces classical overhead in hybrid fault-tolerant workflows.
